The TCP Simulator requires a local ISOLeaf installation.
This feature opens TCP ports on your machine to simulate authorizers and message injectors.
For security reasons, it is not available in the online version.

emvConfig.title: EMV Response Settings
emvConfig.echoDescription: Copies the received Bit 55 directly into the response. Works with any format, including messages with a proprietary header before the TLV.
emvConfig.generateArpcDescription: Derives ARPC using IMK and returns the response Bit 55 with tags 91 and 8A.
emvConfig.proprietaryHeaderTooltip: Some networks insert a proprietary header before the TLV data in Bit 55. Enter the size in bytes of this header so it is skipped before TLV parsing. Examples: 4 bytes = 8 hex chars, 8 bytes = 16 hex chars. If there is no header, leave as 0.
emvConfig.imkOverrideHint: Leave blank to use the IMK configured in Workspace. If no IMK is available, Echo mode will be used as fallback.
emvConfig.validateArqcHint: When enabled, the received ARQC is validated before generating the ARPC. If validation fails, the response will include RC=05 (not authorized) instead of RC=00. Disable to generate ARPC regardless of ARQC validity — useful for integration testing.

simulator.expectLengthPrefixHint: On: the Listener reads 2 length-prefix bytes before each message — standard for acquirer/network connections. Off: reads until the client closes the connection (1 message per connection) — for terminals without framing.

session.framingIncompatibleTooltip: ⚠️ This session expects {{sessionExpects}}, but the Injector is set to {{injectorIncludes}}. Adjust the Injector or pick this session as the destination.

injector.title: Injector
injector.subtitle: Connects to an external TCP system and sends ISO 8583 messages
injector.tpduHint: Leave empty to use Workspace NIIs. Format: 5 bytes = identifier (60) + origin NII (2B) + destination NII (2B). Example: 6000000000.
injector.tpduInvalid: TPDU must be exactly 10 hex characters (5 bytes). Leave empty for auto.
injector.includeLengthPrefixDescription: On: prepends 2 length bytes before the message. Turn off if the target system doesn't expect a length prefix (e.g. POS terminals with proprietary protocols).
injector.detectedPrefixHint: Length prefix {{prefix}} detected and stripped — will be recomputed
injector.framingWarning: Injector: {{injector}} · Listener: {{listener}}. Adjust settings to avoid framing errors.
injector.prefixFromSessionHint: The length prefix follows the selected session's configuration. To control it manually, pick 'Custom destination'.
injector.incompatibleWarning: ⚠️ Incompatible settings: the Injector is set to {{injector}}. The message may not be received correctly if the Listener is not aligned.
injector.noResponses: No responses yet. Configure host/port and inject a message.
injector.varyIdentifiersHelpBody:
On each send, the following fields are refreshed automatically in the message:

• Bit 7 — Transmission DateTime: current date/time
• Bit 11 — STAN: incremented on each send
• Bit 12 — Local Time: current time
• Bit 13 — Local Date: current date
• Bit 37 — RRN: randomly generated

Recommended for continuous mode — prevents the authorizer from rejecting messages as duplicates.
injector.varyAmountHelpBody:
When enabled, Bit 4 (Amount) gets a random value between the configured minimum and maximum on each send.

Useful for simulating real transactional traffic with varied amounts.
injector.amountRangeInvalid: Min must be positive and less than max.

unknownMti.deriveHint: Increments the 3rd digit (ISO 8583 convention). Request→Response (0→1), Advice→Advice Response (2→3), Notification→Notification Response (4→5).
unknownMti.rejectHint: No response is sent. The terminal will time out. Useful for testing error behavior.
unknownMti.echoHint: Responds with the same MTI received. Useful for connectivity debugging.
unknownMti.customHint: Always responds with a specific MTI. Configure it in the field below.
